request.spec:
A plan's amount can be changed (an entry and a save button on the plan; PLAN_CHANGED
name=<person> start=<plan start> amount=<new amount>; a bad amount is refused). The new amount
applies to the claims generated from then on; claims already generated keep theirs. Each plan lists
its changes, oldest first, as <date> amount=<amount>.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
A plan's amount can be changed (an entry and a save button on the plan; PLAN_CHANGED
name=<person> start=<plan start> amount=<new amount>; a bad amount is refused). The new amount
applies to the claims generated from then on; claims already generated keep theirs. Each plan lists
its changes, oldest first, as <date> amount=<amount>.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
You can now change a plan's amount. `bin/e2e` passes all 4 tests in `e2e/specs/acceptance.spec.ts`. (The one "failed" background task was my own wait loop, which I stopped once the run finished. It isn't a test result.)

- **Stored data:** a new migration, `V103__plan_change.sql`, adds a `plan_change` table that keeps each change: its date (the sheet's today when saved) and the new amount. The plan's own amount is updated to the latest one. Generating claims already uses the plan's current amount, so new claims get the new amount and claims already generated keep theirs. When a person is deleted, their plan changes are deleted with them.
- **Server:** a new endpoint, `POST /api/sheets/{sheetId}/plans/{planId}/amount`, built like the existing pause and resume endpoints. As they do, it first refuses viewers, archived sheets and as-of screens. `ChangePlanAmount` checks the amount with the same rule as the add-plan form (more than 0, up to two decimals), so `1.005` is refused with nothing written. On success it writes `PLAN_CHANGED sheet=<id> by=<user> name=<person> start=<plan start> amount=<new amount>` to the audit file. The plans the app returns now include their `changes`, oldest first.
- **Front end:** each plan row in `plans.slot.tsx` now has an amount entry (`plan-amount`), a save button (`plan-amount-save`), and its changes listed as `<date> amount=<amount>` lines (`plan-change-line`). A refused change shows in the row's existing `plan-error` element. The error clears when the entry is edited, saved again, or the plan is paused or resumed.
